extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of philosophy and psychology (academic lecture audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Expository lecture material on methods and criteria for philosophical psychology and metaphysics, arguing for a radical-empiricist, sensation-centered approach to consciousness and for treating superhuman unities as hypotheses. Contains critiques of intellectualism and defenses of Bergson and Fechnerian methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Living understanding over post-mortem conceptual analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy should seek a 'living understanding of the movement of reality,' not follow science in 'vainly patching together fragments of its dead results.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put yourself 'in the making' of things by intuitive sympathy so the whole range of possible decompositions comes into possession; avoid the intellectualist 'post-mortem' method that crawls over works and finds only inconsistencies. Anti-pattern: treating finished products as primary and analyzing them only by abstract concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return to sensation (empiricism) as valid method
rubrics_metrics.description: Remanding us to sensation is a legitimate 'return to empiricism' rather than an ultra-crude regress; sensation reveals realities concepts miss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson's appeal to sensation opens new horizons and gives access to reality's inner life. Do not dismiss appeals to sensation as merely primitive; value direct, sensational acquaintance when seeking insight. Example: Bergson evokes 'the breath of the morning and the song of birds.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and freshness in philosophical writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Good philosophical work should present new horizons and not be 'shop-worn or at second hand.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reiterating 'dusty-minded professors' or turning over 'the same few threadbare categories.' Favor philosophers who 'tell of reality itself' and whose work 'is like the breath of the morning.' Anti-pattern: writings that merely restate previous professors' thoughts without bringing new facts or horizons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid closed systems; philosophy should evoke and invite
rubrics_metrics.description: A closed-in, sealed systematic philosophy is to be distrusted; better is an approach that 'evokes and invites' rather than imposes an intellectualist veto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bergson 'gives us no closed-in system' and is valued for annulling the intellectualist veto. Anti-pattern: judging a philosophy solely by its internal logical closure rather than by its capacity to open the mind and invite new modes of attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concepts are practical instruments, not full equivalents of life
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual or discursive thought is superimposed for practical ends and cannot pretend to reveal life's inner nature; concepts are made for practice, not insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat conceptualization as a tool for navigating life ('to let us jump about over life instead of wading through it') rather than as the final revelation of reality. Method: resist substituting concepts for sensational life when seeking true understanding. Anti-pattern: assuming concepts are the sole avenue to truth ('logos' as sole avenue).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize relations as immediately given (radical empiricism)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relations (time, space, difference, likeness, change, cause, etc.) are integral, immediate members of the sensational flux just as terms are; conjunctions are as real as disjunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject the atomistic intellectualist claim that sensations are purely disjoined. In description and analysis, treat relational content as part of immediate experience rather than as post-conceptual additions. Example: 'The psychology of our own day disavows' the atomistic view; relations are given 'in concreto.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend to continuity and overlap of experience (no atomic moments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience is continuous; the minimal pulses of consciousness 'overflow' their definitions and overlap with past and future and neighboring states—units of experience are not isolated atoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use metaphors like the sliding ruler over dots to model how a sensible experience covers multiple conceptual 'dots' at once. Expect co-consciousness, fringes, subconscious margins, and indefinite radiations rather than strict boundaries. Anti-pattern: treating mental states as temporally or ontologically discrete atoms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use sympathetic intuition—'put yourself in the making'
rubrics_metrics.description: To grasp reality one must 'put yourself in the making' of phenomena by intuitive sympathy rather than only analyzing their completed conceptual forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice inner sympathy to feel how the parts cohere and evolve (Bergson's 'devenir réel'). Seek to follow the movement of life from within; pointing to the 'that' of life can prompt others by inner sympathy to fill out the 'what.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize the primacy of immediate results over mechanistic 'how' questions
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing co-consciousness or co-presence of sensations, focus on the phenomenological results (what is experienced) rather than raising immediately irrelevant questions of how such changes 'come to pass' (e.g., cerebral mechanisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly bracket physiological or causal mechanism when the inquiry is into phenomenological structure; note that the 'immediate condition is probably cerebral' but irrelevant to the present phenomenological account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy should be enacted (an act) not merely talked
rubrics_metrics.description: The return to life is not achieved by talking—'as long as one continues talking, intellectualism remains in undisturbed possession of the field'—philosophy must be exemplified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To induce others to adopt a non-conceptual mode, demonstrate by example (deafen them to talk, point to the 'that' of life). Expect that many minds will refuse to think in non-conceptualized terms; conversion requires persistent personal effort and enactment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat metaphysical unities (the absolute, superhuman consciousness) as hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims about superhuman unities of consciousness (absolute, earth-soul, star-souls) should be treated as plausible hypotheses to be examined inductively, not as logically necessary conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Fechner's method: propose the superhuman consciousness as an hypothesis and recommend it 'by all the resources of induction and persuasion.' Avoid asserting absolute monism by fiat; evaluate probability via analogies and empirical suggestion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empirical analogies and anomalous psychological facts as supporting evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Abnormal or 'supernormal' facts (split personalities, automatic writing, mediumship, possession) and religious experiences can provide suggestive evidence for continuity with a wider spiritual environment and for hypotheses of pooled memories or superhuman co-consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not dismiss these phenomena as irrelevant to metaphysical hypotheses; consider them as part of the evidential stock supporting Fechnerian ideas. But acknowledge their 'spook-haunted' character and proceed decorously when addressing academic audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid assuming monism/pluralism in advance—address probability first
rubrics_metrics.description: Before debating whether a superhuman consciousness is monistic or pluralistic, first ask if any superhuman consciousness is probable at all; do not entangle inquiry in monistic assumptions prematurely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the question of existence (probability) of superhuman unities as primary; only then examine the form (monism vs pluralism). Anti-pattern: using monistic language as a lazy postulate (Fechner's God) that forecloses analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware the scale-shift fallacy in metaphysical defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Intellectualist tactics that try to evade contradictions by invoking a larger-scale absolute merely 'magnify' the same self-contradictions rather than remove them—the absolute will show the same many-in-one contradictions on a vaster scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating absolutist arguments, check whether a purported solution merely repeats the same structural problems at greater magnitude. Example: Bradley's critique of the finite applies equally to an enlarged absolute; do not accept scale-shift as elimination of the original difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophical claims should open new horizons and not merely revive old conceptual objections
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful philosophical move (e.g., Bergson's) will open 'new horizons' and free the philosophical conscience, whereas mere transcendentalist or intellectualist work tends to 'mark time' by reiterating the same objections and answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure philosophical work by whether it yields fresh imaginative insight ('originality, the fecundity, and the imaginative genius') and by its capacity to change the reader's stance ('inner catastrophe') rather than by its conformity to inherited categories. Anti-pattern: works that produce only 'champing of jaws, pawing of the ground.'
